title: Pegula Saves Match Point to Reach WTA Finals Last Four
summary:
Jessica Pegula saved a match point and fought into the last four of the WTA Finals, beating Linda Noskova 7-6, 4-6, 7-5 in a match that swung back and forth.

Pegula had to win: Coco Gauff had beaten Marta Kostyuk earlier on Thursday, so only a win over Noskova would carry her through.

Noskova went a break up in the third set and held a match point on Pegula's serve at 5-4, but she could not take it. Pegula held on and closed out the match, showing great mental resilience.

Pegula's serve was the star of the show. She hit 16 aces, the most she has ever produced in a WTA Tour match, and her returns kept wrong-footing Noskova. Noskova struggled on her own serve, hitting 15 double faults against nine aces.

"I've learned that sometimes the serve feels good and sometimes it doesn't, and how to manage the days when it doesn't and to ride it when you are serving well," Pegula said. "Sometimes there's no rhyme or reason."

Noskova had already secured her semi-final place, where she will face either Elina Svitolina or Aryna Sabalenka on Saturday. Pegula will meet French Open champion Mirra Andreeva next. "It's the match people wanted, well now you are going to get it," Pegula said.

Earlier, Gauff had shown her own fighting spirit to beat Kostyuk. The 22-year-old, the 2024 WTA Finals champion, had treatment on her lower back midway through the match and soon found herself 5-1 down in the second set, but fought back to win. "Physically, I wasn't at my best," Gauff said. "It was like a mental challenge, learning how to play through that." It was the second time Gauff had overturned a 5-1 deficit at this tournament, after doing the same to Pegula on Sunday.
why_it_matters: Saving a match point and winning anyway is one of the most exciting things in sport, and it shows what mental strength can do. For young players, Pegula's win is a lesson in never giving up.
